### Problem

The release candidate v7.19.0 fails the release scenario `conventions-fix` in what the engine did: its `until` or `expect` did not hold, or could no longer hold, so the lane releases nothing and `v7` stays where it is.
Reproduced by: https://github.com/DiluxOne/.github/actions/runs/44677178687 scenario `conventions-fix`.

Cause, verified in the test repository: the review retitled the pull request. On DiluxOne/diluxone-test#3136 the fix round gave the title back as `feat: a greeting, retitled [conventions-fix]` (05:25:36Z), then the review's "type" step (claude-review.yml, `review-type.sh`) read the diff, a fixed change made only of the marker file `scenarios/conventions-fix/retitled.md`, typed it `test` and renamed the pull request to `test: a greeting, retitled [conventions-fix]` (05:26:47Z), so the scenario's `expect` (title `^feat`) cannot hold. The earlier passing runs saw the title before that rename by timing alone (DiluxOne/diluxone-test#3074 was renamed to `test:` too). The fix: in the test repository whose pack says `autopilot: fixed-change`, the review's type of a pull request whose only changed files are its fixed change's files is the issue's type (the title's own type), never `test` from the marker files, so the title is not changed. Test: `review-type.sh` (or the step) keeps `feat` for such a pull request and still corrects the type of any other.

### Scope

- The cause of the failure above, in the engine, fixed with a test that would have caught it.

### Out of scope

- Changing the gates or what they check.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given v7.19.0's candidate with the fix, when the release lane plays `conventions-fix` in the test repository, then it passes and the lane releases it.

### Criticality

Critical
